narrative.text:
Preflight passed: HEAD is exactly `f6e62835`. Upstream main has not moved from `7274283f`. I’ll keep this dormant and avoid attachment/file paths.
The new tests went red (14 failures) and now pass. Group-DM reads are independent of `readJoinedChannels`; writes require both the exact write pin and the relevant scopes. The baseline has no history-membership fallback, so I’m retaining its unknown-key rejection and testing that overlapping fallback input is refused rather than adding that feature here.
I found a scope overlap: the shared write guard also gates uploads and file deletion, so admitting group DMs changes those paths indirectly. I’ve stopped implementation and asked the dispatch manager whether that shared-guard effect is permitted or must remain refused for the parallel change.
The manager approved the shared-guard effect, with file and attachment reads still out of scope. I’ll add real server-path tests for upload admission and file deletion via rollback, without editing either implementation.
Committed as `9592c64`. All six mutations were caught, including separate checks for the group-DM and ordinary-channel guards. The legacy probe matched baseline payload and write-request bytes; it excludes generated checkpoint UUIDs. The required Node-version gates are now running on the clean commit.
All required gates passed on the clean commit: 694 tests on each Node version, typecheck/build on both requested versions, and all 22 new tests five times. The report and logs are written; I’m finalizing the dispatch.
